business_problem: Rent the Runway needed a data platform that could support warehouse automation for garment inspection, sorting, and cleaning so it could replace slow manual processes and deploy an analytics-driven service in only two months.
solution_summary: Rent the Runway built a new warehouse data service on MongoDB Atlas to support robotic garment processing across its fulfillment centers. The engineering team created six dedicated Atlas clusters for services that collect events from X-ray machines, RFID-tagged garments, robotic arms, and smart bins used in cleaning workflows. Those events are copied into RTR’s warehousing environment so engineers and data scientists can analyze units-per-hour performance, tune sorting and cleaning processes, and flag issues such as broken zippers or buttons before they affect the next rental. Atlas’s dynamic schema is especially important because garments carry millions of evolving attributes and cleaning permutations, and the team needed to ingest that data while iterating rapidly with automation hardware. MongoDB’s managed infrastructure let RTR focus on analytics, integration, and process redesign instead of running database operations during a race to production.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores warehouse automation events and powers the analytics and application logic behind RTR’s robotic garment-processing workflows.

data_flow: X-ray machines, RFID-tagged garments, robotic arms, and smart bins generate events that are stored in MongoDB Atlas, copied into RTR’s warehousing system, and analyzed in real time to guide sorting, cleaning, and quality interventions.
business_outcome: RTR reduced garment-processing time by two thirds, maintained 100% uptime through a cloud migration, expanded cleaning techniques, and gained a scalable, zero-maintenance data foundation for warehouse automation.
metrics: RTR gives customers access to items from more than 800 designer brands.
The result is a 67% decrease in processing time compared to manually checking each garment.
